keyFindings.text: **P1 — `bots activity --json`'s row shape is never specified by its producer, but its consumer parses six status values out of it.** 001's REQ-002 promises only "each group carrying its id, its title and its rows" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:144], and its acceptance criterion repeats the same three fields [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/acceptance-criteria.md:55]. 003 draws "each with one of six markers: `·` running, `✓` done, `✗` failed, `!` needs input, `–` cancelled, `?` stale" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:168] and its AC-005 asserts a done row carries `✓` and `done` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/acceptance-criteria.md:43]. Nothing names the row's `state`, `botId`, `at` or `actor` fields. **Exact edit**: extend 001 REQ-002 to "each row carrying `botId`, `identity`, `state`, `at`, `actor` and `runId`", and add the same list to AC-002.

**P1 — 001 adds `actor` to the run record without saying where it goes, and the record validator refuses any schema version but 1.** `RunRecord` declares `schemaVersion: 1` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/run-record.ts:197] and `validateRunRecord` returns `record-schema-unsupported` for anything else [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/run-record.ts:239], while `FIELD_GROUPS` is a closed list of eight groups [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/run-record.ts:218]. 001's affected-surfaces table says `run-record.ts` gains "the field, its check and its null default" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:76] but never says top-level or inside `identity`, and never says how a record written before the phase stays readable. A bump to 2 would make every existing record unreadable and `bots status --rebuild` would drop them. **Exact edit**: add to 001's plan "`actor` is a nullable top-level field, `schemaVersion` stays 1, and `actor.vitest.ts` asserts a record written before this phase still validates".

**P1 — 011 lands `operators.json` while the parent's Out of Scope forbids any child from building it, and 011's justification cites a parent edit that was never made.** The parent says "The rest of the small-team model (§12): two roles in one `operators.json` and a shared host at mode 0770. No child builds them; 001 lands the actor field alone" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:94]. 011 decides "yes, the minimal roster" and asserts "the parent's phase-map row records it" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281], but the 011 phase-map row names only "a file-backed identity link" and the 001/006/008/010 dependencies [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:131]. **Exact edit**: replace `spec.md:94` with "The two-role `operators.json` and the shared-host 0770 mode: 001 lands the actor field alone, and 011 lands the minimal `owner`/`members` roster its approver check needs", and add "the `operators.json` roster" to the 011 row at `spec.md:131`.

**P1 — the build order puts the approval overlay (003) before the grant vocabulary (006) and no phase revisits it.** 003 is phase 3 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:123] and 006 is phase 6 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:126]. 010 is the only later phase that edits the crate, and it edits `cli.rs` for chat only [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:120]. So the screen's approval path is frozen at pre-006 semantics. **Exact edit**: add a 006 task "Update `crates/bots-tui/src/render/overlay.rs` and `keys.rs` to the four scopes and the `--scope` write", and add `crates/bots-tui` to 006's Files to Change table.

**P1 — the parent spec still describes ten phases while the phase map lists eleven.** The title and description say "Ten build phases" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:3], §3 In Scope says "The ten ranked slices ... one child phase each" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:78], the Files to Change preamble says "the ten phases touch" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:100], and the Handoff Criteria still say "010-conversations closes the program" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:55], while the phase map carries an eleventh row for `011-messaging-channels/` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:131]. 011 itself says it "extends the program rather than continuing its order" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:43]. **Exact edit**: change `spec.md:3` to "Eleven build phases", `spec.md:78` to "The ten ranked slices ... plus the messaging-channels extension", `spec.md:100` to "the eleven phases touch", and `spec.md:55` to "011-messaging-channels closes the program".

**P1 — the parent's Files to Change table omits every 011 surface.** The `bots.cjs` row lists phases "001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:104], the runtime row says "001-010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:105], and the `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row lists "001, 002, 008, 009, 010" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:109], yet 011 adds a `bots channel` verb group [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:155], five `channel-*.ts` runtime modules [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:137-140] and Apache-2.0 notices for rakazo and turnstone [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:160]. **Exact edit**: append `011` to the phase column of `spec.md:104`, change `spec.md:105` to "001-011", and append `011` to `spec.md:109`.

**P1 — three phases define three incompatible grammars for answering one needs-you item.** 003 answers through `bots answer` with free text and binds `y` to `approve`, `a` to `always`, `n` to `deny` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:171], and its overlay draws `1 approve once`, `2 approve always`, `n deny` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:174]. 006 adds `bots answer --scope once|conversation|always|deny` and records the scope on the grant [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:96]. 011 sends "the item's `options`, which the runner fills from the `[OPTION]` lines" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:179]. The runtime does carry `options: string[] | null` on the item [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:38] and the marker exists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/dispatch.ts:45], so 011's path is buildable; 003's is not, because `bots answer` accepts no options at all today [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:73]. Consequences: 003's "approve always" records no standing allow, and 006's `conversation` scope has no surface anywhere. **Exact edit**: add to 003 REQ-003 "the write is `bots answer <item-id> <text> --scope <once|always|deny>`", rewrite 003 REQ-006/REQ-009 to the four scopes, and add to 011 REQ-007 "a chosen option maps to the scope 006 names, and an item with no options gets `once`/`deny`".

**P2 — the child docs repeat the stale phase count, and 003 calls `bots status --json` a producer of a field it does not emit.** 003's metadata says "Phase 3 of 10" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:31]. 003's plan names `bots status --json` as "Producer of the header's bot count and staleness flag" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/plan.md:85], but the payload is `{indexPath, builtAt, stale, staleIdentities, rows, duplicateRoots, notes}` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status.ts:417] — the staleness flag exists, the bot count is a count of `rows` where `kind` is `bot`. **Exact edit**: change `003-terminal-screen/spec.md:31` to "Phase 3 of 11", and change `003-terminal-screen/plan.md:85` to "Producer of the header's staleness flag and the rows the bot count is counted from".

**P2 — the routine sentence has no owner.** 002's `--json` is specified to carry "its `what`, rendered starts, `does`, `until`, `untilMetAt`, failure streak and switch state" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:171], while 003 draws "the bot id, the four-part routine sentence and the routine's state" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:170]. Neither says who renders the sentence, so 003 re-implements 002's text rendering and the two can drift. **Exact edit**: add `sentence` to 002 REQ-007's field list, or change 003 REQ-007 to "composes the sentence from `what`, `starts`, `does` and `until`".

**P1 — 008's mitigation for the dispatch-env gate cannot be implemented as written.** 008's risk row says "Widen `assertDispatchEnvAllowed` with the `SKILLED_BOT_SECRET_` prefix in the same change" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:187]. That function admits only exact keys from a per-kind list: `if (!allowed.includes(key)) throw new Error(...)` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-audit.ts:1508-1517], and the env the bots runtime passes is already filtered by `isAllowedExecutorEnvKey` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-audit.ts:1155] through `dispatchEnv: built.env` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/dispatch.ts:601-612]. A prefix is admitted by neither, so the secret never reaches the child. **Exact edit**: replace the risk row with "`isAllowedExecutorEnvKey` and `assertDispatchEnvAllowed` both gain a `SKILLED_BOT_SECRET_` prefix rule scoped to the bots dispatch path, and a test asserts `PATH` and a non-prefixed key are still refused".

**P1 — 011 reads the token at send time, but two transports need it before any send.** REQ-014 reads the value "at send time" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:191], while Telegram long polling [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:181] and Slack `apps.connections.open` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:182] need it to open the connection. A transport that resolves the token only when sending cannot start. **Exact edit**: change REQ-014 to "read at `start` and at every send, and never held in a field that outlives the call".

**P1 — approval authority is split three ways and no phase states the model.** 011 gates a channel answer on `owner` or `members` in `operators.json` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177]; 003 writes `bots answer` with no check at all [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:162]; 006's ladder takes kinds, rules, auto-review and extra-vigilant as inputs and no actor [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:96]. So a channel answer is gated and a terminal answer is not, and nothing says why. **Exact edit**: add one sentence to 006's scope: "The host is the authority: a terminal answer needs no roster because it needs the state root. A channel answer adds the `operators.json` roster 011 lands." and have 003 REQ-003 cite it.

**P1 — inbound chat text becomes the run prompt with no untrusted framing.** 010 appends the transcript after the BOT.md body as the request prompt [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:148], and 011 routes any line that is not an answer into that path [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:192]. A chat message is therefore an instruction the bot will follow, from anyone in the chat. No phase says the transcript is data. **Exact edit**: add to 010 REQ-001 "the transcript sits under a fixed `## Conversation` heading that states the lines are untrusted user text and not instructions", and have 011 REQ-015 cite that heading.

**P1 — the `always` scope does not outlive its item, but two surfaces label a control "always".** 006 states "A saved rule that outlives its item - rung 2 has no store in this phase, so an `always` scope is recorded on the item and read by the resumed prompt, not by a later item" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:104]. 003 binds `a` to `always` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:171] and draws `2 approve always` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:174]. The operator reads "always" and gets "this run". **Exact edit**: change 003 REQ-006/REQ-009 to `a` → `approve for this run` and `2 approve for this run`, or add the rule store to 006 and say so in its scope.

**P1 — the grant scope is not part of the answer's identity, so a second answer with the same text and a different scope is silently dropped.** `answerItem` refuses only when the text differs: `if (state === 'answered' && item.answer?.text !== input.text) return { ok: false, reason: 'item-answered-differently' }` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/answer.ts:85]. 006 adds `--scope once|conversation|always|deny` and "records the scope on the grant" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:96], but never says the scope joins the comparison. So `bots answer item-1 yes --scope once` followed by `bots answer item-1 yes --scope always` returns `duplicate` and the standing allow is lost with no error. **Exact edit**: add to 006 REQ "the answer's identity is its text and its scope: a second answer with the same text and a different scope is refused `item-answered-differently`", and change `answer.ts:85` to compare both fields.

**P1 — the Telegram bot token travels in the request URL and no requirement redacts it.** 011 REQ-009 long-polls `getUpdates` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:181], and the Bot API puts the token in the path — the reference implementation builds `https://api.telegram.org/bot123:ABC/getMe` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_tests.rs:268]. 011 REQ-014 says only that the value is "read from the store at send time and never written to the channel config, a queue entry, a log or a run record" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:191], which does not cover a URL rendered inside an error string. **Exact edit**: add to 011 REQ-009 "every URL is rendered with the token replaced by `bot<redacted>` before it reaches an error, a log or a queue entry", and add a test that a failed `getUpdates` prints no token.

**P2 — an `unknown` send is never retried and never surfaced.** 011 REQ-013 records an uncertain send `unknown` and never retries it [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:185], and `bots channel list` reports only queue depth [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:196]. A lost approval prompt is therefore invisible. **Exact edit**: add to REQ-019 "`bots channel list` prints the count of `unknown` entries, and `bots channel drain --report` lists them with their idempotency key".

**P2 — the approval index has no expiry and no removal rule.** 011 REQ-006 writes an entry per prompt before the send [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:178] and no requirement removes it, so the file grows without bound and a stale entry can resolve a press for an item answered hours ago. **Exact edit**: add to REQ-006 "an entry is removed when its item is answered or expired, and a press naming a missing entry is refused `channel-prompt-unknown`".

**P1 — 001's version bump makes an existing index unreadable, and the rebuild it relies on is not a requirement.** The index refuses a stored version that differs: `if (row?.value !== SCHEMA_VERSION) throw new Error(...)` and the caller returns `index-unreadable` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts:253-258]. 001's risk row says the mitigation is "Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`, rebuild from run records on open, and prove it with a test that opens a version-2 index" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:179], but no requirement in 001 states the rebuild-on-open behaviour, so an implementer can satisfy every REQ and still leave `bots status` failing on an old index. **Exact edit**: add to 001's P0 table "REQ-008: an index whose stored version differs from `SCHEMA_VERSION` is rebuilt from run records on open, and `bots status` prints no error", and cite it from the risk row.

**P1 — 004 requires the index schema version to stay `'2'`, but 001 (phase 1) bumps it to `'3'`.** 004's REQ-006 says "`SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `'2'`, so an index built before this phase still opens" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/spec.md:147], and both its readiness check and its affected-surfaces row assert `rg -n "SCHEMA_VERSION = '2'"` prints one line [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/plan.md:49] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/plan.md:82]. 001 bumps it: "Add the `actor` column, bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:114] and its verification expects `'3'` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:76]. 004 is phase 4, so its readiness check fails on the first day and its requirement is false. **Exact edit**: change 004 REQ-006 to "this phase adds no column and no version change; the index version is whatever 001 left", and replace the literal `'2'` in `004-computer-exposure/plan.md:49,82` with "the version 001 left".

**P1 — 007 and 008 both need the deep-loop dispatch-env allowlist and neither names the edit precisely enough to make.** 007 sets `UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` in the child environment and says it is "admitting that key through the deep-loop executor allowlist" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:99], without naming which executor kinds. 008 says "Widen `assertDispatchEnvAllowed` with the `SKILLED_BOT_SECRET_` prefix" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:187]. That function admits exact keys only: `if (!allowed.includes(key)) throw new Error(...)` against a per-kind list [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-audit.ts:1495-1517], so a prefix is refused there. **Exact edit**: state the edit once, in 007: "`DISPATCH_ENV_KEYS` gains `UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` for every kind, and `assertDispatchEnvAllowed` gains a prefix rule mirroring `EXECUTOR_ENV_PREFIXES_BY_KIND`", and have 008 cite it for `SKILLED_BOT_SECRET_`.

**P1 — correction to iteration 2's finding 9: the prefix machinery already exists on the parent-env side, so only one of the two filters needs a new rule.** Iteration 2 said "a prefix is admitted by neither". That is wrong for the parent-env filter: `isAllowedExecutorEnvKey` already ends with `return (EXECUTOR_ENV_PREFIXES_BY_KIND[kind] ?? []).some((prefix) => key.startsWith(prefix))` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-audit.ts:317]. The core claim stands — `assertDispatchEnvAllowed` is exact-match, so 008's mitigation as written fails — but the fix is smaller than iteration 2 implied: add `SKILLED_BOT_SECRET_` to `EXECUTOR_ENV_PREFIXES_BY_KIND` for every kind and mirror the prefix rule in `assertDispatchEnvAllowed`. **Exact edit**: none in the packet; this corrects the evidence in `iteration-002.md` finding 9 and supersedes its "neither" clause.

**P1 — four phases edit `answer.ts` and no phase states that the edits compose.** 001 writes `by` on the answer [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:146], 006 writes the scope on the grant [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:96], 009 adds a proposal seam that "call[s] the proposal seam before the resume enqueue, and report[s] a recorded review instead of a request" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:125], and 011 reuses the path for channel answers [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:49]. The function is one linear body: read, refuse, write the answer, build the resume request, enqueue, stamp [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/answer.ts:68-120]. 009's "instead of a request" is a branch in the middle of that body, and nothing says whether it runs before or after 006's scope write. **Exact edit**: add to 009's plan "the seam runs after the answer and the scope are written and before the resume request is built, and a test asserts one answer carries `by`, the scope and the recorded review".

**P1 — four phases edit one prompt builder and no phase states the order of its sections.** `buildBotPrompt` builds a fixed line list: the child exemption, the bound spec folder, the optional checkout line, the decision marker, then the body [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/dispatch.ts:315-338]. 004 adds a working-place line [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/spec.md:142], 005 prepends the memory block [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:94], 009 adds skill bodies [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:102], and 010 appends the transcript after the body [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:148].
